description: Ordered step manifest for the deployment regression scenario (AGT-2739). This file is data: id, title, level, and the outcome a reader should expect. The assertions themselves are typed C# in ScenarioSteps.cs, keyed by id. `smoke` runs every smoke-level step (1-7) in order; `full` runs all steps in order.

steps.title: Bootstrap principals
steps.description: Issue a runner principal credential from a freshly started Task Server.
steps.expectedOutcome: POST /api/v1/management/principals returns a bearer credential for a coding-runner identity.

steps.title: Register runner
steps.description: Start the real runner binary against the Task Server using the issued credential.
steps.expectedOutcome: GET /api/v1/runners lists the runner id before it claims any work.

steps.title: Create task
steps.description: Create the seeded workspace, project, and one ready task from fixture.json.

steps.title: Claim task
steps.description: The runner polls and claims the ready task under a fenced lease.
steps.expectedOutcome: Exactly one run is created and audited as work.permit.accepted.

steps.title: Run with the fake CLI
steps.description: The runner drives the fake coding CLI, which reports the fixture's known-passing and known-failing checks, commits, and pushes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The task reaches 4-auto-review with an immutable result handoff, a new commit lands on the seeded repository's immutable result ref, and the run's evidence artifacts include a results log naming both checks. In Compose, Studio BFF stays stopped during the run.

steps.title: Run with the fake CLI on the legacy runner plane
steps.description: The same coding attempt on the plane the production fleet uses (AGT-2985): the backend monolith, a second real runner, and the fixture repository served over smart HTTP run as sibling processes; the runner claims over /api/runner/claim (no run id) and completes over /api/runner/completion with session-continuation evidence.
steps.expectedOutcome: The completion is accepted and the task reaches 4-auto-review; the continuation ledger entry names the server's fenced attempt id, which differs from the lease id; the runner never logs 'Session continuation evidence does not match'; a new commit lands on the fixture repository.

steps.title: Auto-review
steps.description: The real review executor materializes and checks the completed coding run, reports and cleans up. After Pass, a supervised fixture publisher fast-forwards canonical main to the reviewed SHA and verifies the remote ref.
steps.expectedOutcome: The same task reaches 5-human-review and the canonical fixture ref equals the reviewed SHA while Studio BFF remains stopped in Compose.

steps.title: Orchestrator chat turn with context receipt
steps.description: Append an orchestrator chat turn for the task and read back its context receipt.
steps.expectedOutcome: The appended turn is readable and its receipt reports a token budget and at least one source.

steps.title: Backup
steps.description: Create a management backup of the running Task Server's store.
steps.expectedOutcome: POST /api/v1/management/backups returns a backup id, path, and SHA-256 file digest.

steps.title: Restore into an empty store, inventory hash equality
steps.description: Start a second Task Server instance against a fresh, empty data directory, place the backup file where it expects one, put it in Maintenance mode, and restore.
steps.expectedOutcome: POST /api/v1/management/restore reports the restored file's SHA-256 equal to the source backup's SHA-256 (inventory hash equality).

knownGaps.reason: The distributed Task Server / Studio BFF / Runner topology this scenario boots has no dossier or decision-gate concept yet; it exists only in the separate backend monolith. Tracked as future scenario growth once that concept lands in this topology.

Since AGT-2890 the runner uploads result artifacts after the fenced completion. The v1 Task Server admits that with the outbox authority; the backend monolith answers 409 'RunAttempt is Completed', so a legacy-plane run ships no result artifacts. The legacy step therefore asserts completion acceptance, not artifacts.
task-server has no native 6-completed/7-archive transition; those states are written only by the backend monolith. The auto-review step's 5-human-review is the current ceiling for this topology.
